Test uses a single typical value (2450) and does not exercise boundary values such as 0, negative, or MAX; no empty/zero/negative cases are tested.
The test is short and self-contained (<10 lines) with no repeated logic in this single test; no helper methods are needed for this single simple case.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is small (well under 20 lines) and contains no loops or conditionals, following a simple linear Arrange-Act-Assert pattern.

Only one assertion is made (a single numeric equality). The assertion is superficial for object state: it verifies only the count and does not check additional properties that would increase fault detection.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations and no commented-out @Test methods; the test is active and runnable.
The test method and class lack any annotations, Javadoc, or comments linking the test to requirements/ticket IDs (no @Story, @Requirement, or REQ- markers).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: A timeout is specified (@Test(timeout = 4000)), indicating an explicit performance-related constraint in the unit test. Therefore an explicit performance assertion exists.
The method name 'test7' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome; it lacks the recommended descriptive naming convention.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The file includes an auto-generated header comment ('This file was automatically generated by EvoSuite'), indicating heavy test generation and reduced intention-revealing clarity.
practices_evaluation.original_code:
/*
 * This file was automatically generated by EvoSuite
 * Tue Aug 04 21:02:44 GMT 2020
 */
...

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: No Given-When-Then structure, BDD naming, or multiple scenario coverage is present; the test appears minimal and likely written after implementation rather than in a prioritized, design-first manner.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API (constructor and numVertices) and does not access private fields or use reflection, so it verifies observable behavior rather than implementation details.
The test uses a specific assertion assertEquals with a descriptive failure message; the assertion is specific rather than generic (not just assertTrue), meeting the guidance for clear assertions.
There are minimal comments, no commented-out code, and the only inline text is a useful assertion message; no excessive or misleading comments are present.
The test contains no sources of nondeterminism (no Random, no time calls, no Thread.sleep) and uses deterministic constructor and accessor, so results should be reproducible.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: Test uses only local variables and does not create external resources or modify static/shared state; there is no persistence or resource leakage visible in the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing categorization at class level and enabling selective execution.
